findings.title: isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is always False for SpawnProcess
findings.body: `self.mp_context` is created with `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")`, so `self.mp_context.Process(...)` returns a `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` instance. In CPython's `multiprocessing` module, `SpawnProcess` subclasses `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process` (they are sibling classes). As a result, `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` on lines 254 and 346 always evaluates to `False` at runtime. When a flusher process hangs (`cause == "hang"`), `_ensure_processes_alive()` never kills the hung process before spawning a replacement, leaving duplicate processes flushing the same shards concurrently; similarly, `join()` never terminates still-running processes on shutdown. Check `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess)` or `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)` instead.

findings.title: join() breaks out of the loop on timeout without terminating remaining processes
findings.body: In `SpanFlusher.join()`, if `deadline` is reached while waiting in `self.next_step.join(timeout)` or while waiting for an earlier process in `self.processes`, the check `if remaining_time <= 0: break` exits the `for` loop immediately. Any subsequent processes in `self.processes` are skipped and never terminated. The `while process.is_alive() and (deadline is None or deadline > time.time()):` loop on line 343 already avoids sleeping once the deadline has passed, so removing the early `break` (and only calling `process.terminate()` when `process.is_alive()`) ensures all remaining processes are cleaned up when the timeout expires.

findings.title: submit() queries cluster-wide Redis memory info once per flusher process and creates duplicate Redis clients
findings.body: `SpansBuffer.get_memory_info()` queries `INFO memory` across all nodes in the Redis cluster and is not scoped to `assigned_shards`. By storing each child's `shard_buffer` in `self.buffers` and calling `buffer.get_memory_info()` for every entry in `self.buffers.values()` on each `submit()`, the main consumer process opens `num_processes` extra Redis connection pools and executes `INFO memory` against the entire Redis cluster `num_processes` times per batch instead of once. Keeping `self.buffer = buffer` from `__init__` (which already covers all assigned shards) and calling `self.buffer.record_stored_segments()` and `self.buffer.get_memory_info()` once avoids the redundant network calls and extra client pools in the parent process.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag key ('shards' vs 'shard') and high-cardinality tag values when sharing processes
findings.body: Lines 185 and 195 tag `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` with `tags={"shard": shard_tag}`, whereas line 199 tags `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` with `tags={"shards": shard_tag}`. In addition, when multiple shards share a process (which is the default since `--flusher-processes` defaults to 1), `shard_tag = ",".join(map(str, shards))` concatenates the consumer's assigned partition subset into a single tag value that changes across Kafka rebalances, creating high-cardinality metric tags.
